# LoreCanvas UI/UX Master Specification & Implementation Template

```text
LORECANVAS
UI/UX MASTER SPECIFICATION

DOCUMENT PURPOSE

This document defines the complete UI/UX direction for LoreCanvas.

The purpose is to design and implement the frontend of LoreCanvas while preserving the existing backend, domain models, repositories, storage systems, commands, graph systems, timeline systems, map systems, and other completed functionality.

The UI must adapt to the existing architecture rather than forcing architectural changes.

==================================================
1. CORE IMPLEMENTATION RULES
==================================================

1. The existing backend is the source of truth.

2. DO NOT rewrite, replace, restructure, or remove completed backend systems.

3. DO NOT create duplicate frontend-specific versions of backend data.

4. UI components must communicate with the existing domain/repository APIs.

5. Do not introduce new backend systems merely to simplify frontend implementation.

6. If a required UI feature cannot currently be supported by the backend:
   - identify the limitation,
   - do not silently modify the backend,
   - propose the smallest compatible interface/extension,
   - wait for authorization before changing completed backend architecture.

7. Preserve existing:
   - domain models
   - repositories
   - storage
   - commands
   - undo/redo
   - search
   - graph functionality
   - timeline functionality
   - map functionality
   - plugin infrastructure
   - data relationships
   - persistence behavior

8. Do not remove existing functionality simply because a new UI design provides a different way to access it.

9. UI redesigns must remain compatible with future multiplatform development.

10. Keep business logic out of UI components wherever the existing architecture provides appropriate services/repositories.

11. Prefer reusable UI components over duplicated implementations.

12. Do not add features merely because they seem useful.
    Implement the specification.

==================================================
2. UI DESIGN PHILOSOPHY
==================================================

LoreCanvas should feel like:

- a writing application,
- a worldbuilding workspace,
- a story planning tool,
- and a connected knowledge environment.

It should NOT feel like:

- a database administration panel,
- a complicated RPG character editor,
- a collection of unrelated tools,
- or a mandatory worldbuilding questionnaire.

Core principle:

"The writer should be able to write immediately, while advanced worldbuilding remains available when wanted."

The interface should therefore support two experiences:

SIMPLE MODE
    Write immediately.
    Minimal setup.
    Minimal interface complexity.

COMPLEX MODE
    Full worldbuilding environment.
    Characters.
    Nations.
    Locations.
    Organizations.
    Species.
    Magic systems.
    Maps.
    Timeline.
    Relationships.
    Other worldbuilding systems.

Both modes use the same underlying application architecture and data systems.

==================================================
3. UI LAYER ARCHITECTURE
==================================================

Design the frontend in the following conceptual layers:

LAYER 1: CORE NAVIGATION

    Home / Story Library
    Story Workspace
    Writing
    World
    Maps
    Timeline
    Relationships
    Settings

LAYER 2: STORY INTERACTION

    Story Sidebar
    Character Review Cards
    Map Context
    Timeline Context
    World Context
    Relationship Context

LAYER 3: CREATION TOOLS

    Quick Add
    Editors
    Forms
    Templates
    Custom Fields
    Context Menus

LAYER 4: PRODUCTIVITY

    Search
    Command Palette
    Keyboard Shortcuts
    Autosave Feedback
    Undo/Redo
    History
    Recovery

LAYER 5: PRESENTATION

    Themes
    Custom Background
    Reader Mode
    Focus Mode
    Export
    Accessibility

LAYER 6: PLATFORM UX

    Mobile layouts
    Desktop layouts
    Touch interaction
    Keyboard/mouse interaction
    Responsive panels
    Future multiplatform compatibility

==================================================
4. STORY LIBRARY / HOME
==================================================

Design a simple Story Library.

It should allow the writer to:

- create a story,
- open a story,
- search stories,
- sort stories,
- favorite/pin stories,
- continue recently edited stories,
- delete/archive stories where supported.

The Home screen should prioritize:

    Continue Writing
    Recent Stories
    Favorite Stories
    Create New Story

Do not make the home screen an overwhelming statistics dashboard.

==================================================
5. STORY CREATION
==================================================

Story creation must support:

SIMPLE MODE

The writer can enter:

    Story Name
    Optional Description

Then immediately begin writing.

COMPLEX MODE

The writer may optionally configure:

    Characters
    World
    Nations
    Locations
    Organizations
    Species
    Magic Systems
    Maps
    Timeline
    Relationships
    Other worldbuilding information

Complex Mode must NOT require the writer to fill everything before writing.

The writer must always be able to return to writing.

==================================================
6. STORY WORKSPACE
==================================================

The Story Workspace is the central environment of LoreCanvas.

It should contain:

    Story Navigation
    Story Editor
    Optional Story Sidebar
    Contextual tools

The Story Editor must remain visually dominant.

Worldbuilding tools must support the writing process rather than constantly obstruct it.

==================================================
7. WRITING EDITOR
==================================================

Design the editor around:

    Chapters
    Scenes
    Story text
    Autosave
    Word count
    Editing
    Undo/Redo
    Focus Mode

The editor should support a distraction-free writing experience.

Do not force worldbuilding panels into the writer's face.

The writer should be able to collapse contextual UI.

==================================================
8. STORY SIDEBAR
==================================================

Create an optional Story Sidebar inspired by sidebar-based productivity browsers.

The sidebar is a secondary contextual workspace.

It must NOT replace the story editor.

It can be opened and closed while writing or reading.

Primary sidebar sections:

    PEOPLE
    PLACE
    WORLD
    TIMELINE
    CONNECTIONS

The sidebar displays information relevant to the writer's current story position where possible.

The sidebar should remember its last selected section when practical.

==================================================
9. PEOPLE / ACTIVE CHARACTERS
==================================================

The People section should prioritize characters currently relevant to the story position.

Example:

    ACTIVE CHARACTERS

    Elara Varen
    Kael Varen
    Mira

Character cards are REVIEW interfaces.

They are NOT the full character editor.

Tapping a character card should provide a concise overview.

Possible information:

    Portrait
    Name
    Role
    Status
    Relevant relationships
    Current location
    Relevant information

Provide:

    Open Full Character

when the writer wants deeper information.

==================================================
10. CHARACTER SYSTEM UI
==================================================

Character management must have two distinct experiences.

CHARACTER EDITOR

Used to create and modify the character.

CHARACTER REVIEW CARD

Used while reading/writing to quickly remember the character.

Character Editor may contain:

    Identity
    Appearance
    Personality
    Background
    Abilities
    Motivations
    Strengths
    Weaknesses
    Secrets
    Relationships
    Timeline
    Locations
    Organizations
    Custom Fields
    Notes

Do not force every field to be completed.

Use progressive disclosure and collapsible sections.

Provide:

    + Add Attribute
    + Add Note
    + Add Relationship

where appropriate.

==================================================
11. WORLD UI
==================================================

Worldbuilding must be organized clearly.

Potential categories:

    Characters
    Nations
    Locations
    Organizations
    Species
    Magic System
    Lore
    Other supported worldbuilding entities

Do not force every category into Simple Mode.

Complex Mode exposes the complete environment.

==================================================
12. MAP UI
==================================================

The existing MapMaker is part of the application's worldbuilding environment.

The UI must allow writers to:

    Open maps
    Navigate maps
    Inspect locations
    Inspect nations
    View relevant entities
    Return to the story

Map context can be surfaced through the Story Sidebar.

Provide:

    Current Location
    View on Map

when a story position has an associated location.

Do not duplicate map data in the UI.

Use existing map/domain functionality.

==================================================
13. TIMELINE UI
==================================================

The existing Timeline system should be integrated into:

    Timeline workspace
    Story Sidebar
    Character pages
    Story context

A character can display relevant timeline events without creating duplicate timeline data.

Timeline events should link back to the existing Timeline system.

==================================================
14. RELATIONSHIP / GRAPH UI
==================================================

Use the existing relationship/graph architecture.

The UI should provide:

    Relationship list
    Character relationships
    Entity relationships
    Local graph
    Expanded graph
    Full graph where appropriate

Default graphs should be focused.

Do NOT immediately display hundreds of unrelated entities.

Allow:

    Expand
    Collapse
    Open Entity
    View Relationship

Take inspiration from knowledge-graph interfaces such as Obsidian while keeping LoreCanvas's identity.

==================================================
15. STORY CONTEXT
==================================================

LoreCanvas should recognize that the writer's current story position can provide contextual information.

Where supported by existing data, the interface may display:

    Current Characters
    Current Location
    Current Nation
    Current Event
    Current Timeline Position
    Relevant Organizations
    Relevant World Information

This information should be presented through the Story Sidebar.

==================================================
16. READER EXPERIENCE
==================================================

LoreCanvas should also support reading the story.

While reading:

    Story remains central.
    Story Sidebar remains optional.
    Character Review Cards remain accessible.
    Map context remains accessible.
    Timeline context remains accessible.

Avoid exposing unnecessary editing controls in reading mode.

==================================================
17. SPOILER-AWARE CONTEXT
==================================================

When reading a story, future information must not automatically be exposed when a contextual system is designed to represent current story knowledge.

Where the existing data model supports it, distinguish between:

    Information known at current story position
    Complete author information

The author must be able to access complete information when appropriate.

Do not implement a complex spoiler system by modifying backend architecture without authorization.

==================================================
18. QUICK ADD
==================================================

Provide a global Quick Add mechanism.

Example:

    + Create

    Character
    Location
    Nation
    Organization
    Species
    Timeline Event
    Map
    Relationship
    Note
    Chapter
    Scene

Only show options supported by the current application state.

Quick Add should be available from appropriate contexts.

==================================================
19. SEARCH
==================================================

Create a unified search experience.

Search should eventually be able to find:

    Characters
    Locations
    Nations
    Organizations
    Species
    Timeline Events
    Relationships
    Chapters
    Story text
    Notes
    Other supported entities

Search results should identify the entity type.

Example:

    ELARA VAREN
    Character

    ARCLIGHT
    Location

    SIEGE OF ARCLIGHT
    Timeline Event

Do not create a second independent data/search system if the backend already provides search functionality.

==================================================
20. COMMAND PALETTE
==================================================

On desktop, provide a command palette where appropriate.

Potential shortcut:

    Ctrl/Cmd + K

Possible commands:

    Create Character
    Create Location
    Open Map
    Open Timeline
    Find Character
    Open Story
    Add Relationship
    Search
    Toggle Sidebar
    Toggle Focus Mode
    Open Settings

Mobile should provide an equivalent accessible action interface.

==================================================
21. FOCUS MODE
==================================================

Provide a distraction-free writing mode.

Focus Mode should minimize:

    Navigation
    Worldbuilding UI
    Sidebar
    Unnecessary controls

The story editor becomes the primary visual element.

The writer can exit Focus Mode at any time.

==================================================
22. APPEARANCE SYSTEM
==================================================

Settings must provide:

    Theme
    Accent / visual preferences where supported
    Background

Supported themes:

    Light
    Dark
    System

==================================================
23. CUSTOM BACKGROUND
==================================================

Add:

Settings
    → Appearance
        → Background

Allow writers to import an image from their device.

The imported image becomes the LoreCanvas application background.

Provide:

    Choose Image
    Replace Image
    Remove Image
    Preview

Where practical also provide:

    Opacity
    Blur
    Position/Crop

The background must not compromise text readability.

The UI should provide appropriate content surfaces/contrast above the image.

The feature must remain offline.

Do not introduce online wallpaper services.

Do not introduce video or animated backgrounds unless explicitly requested later.

The custom background is a global application appearance setting.

Do not automatically make it story-specific.

==================================================
24. SETTINGS
==================================================

Settings should eventually contain:

    Account
    Appearance
    Writing
    Editor
    Storage
    Export
    Accessibility
    About

Keep Settings organized and understandable.

Avoid exposing technical backend settings to ordinary writers.

==================================================
25. EXPORT / PUBLISHING UI
==================================================

The UI must expose the existing export/publishing capabilities.

Potential output types include:

    EPUB
    PDF
    DOCX
    Markdown
    Other supported formats

Where supported, completed stories should be able to include appropriate worldbuilding material such as:

    Maps
    Illustrations
    Other selected story assets

Export should provide a clear workflow.

Example:

    Export
      ↓
    Choose Format
      ↓
    Configure
      ↓
    Preview
      ↓
    Export

Do not assume unsupported formats are implemented.

Use existing backend/export functionality.

==================================================
26. ACCESSIBILITY
==================================================

Design for:

    Adjustable text size
    Good contrast
    Clear touch targets
    Keyboard navigation
    Screen-reader compatibility where platform supports it
    Reduced motion
    Readable typography
    Clear focus indicators

Accessibility must not be treated as a final cosmetic step.

==================================================
27. OFFLINE UX
==================================================

LoreCanvas is offline-first.

The UI should clearly communicate:

    Saved
    Saving
    Unsaved changes
    Recovery
    Export progress
    Import progress
    Errors

Do not require internet access for core writing and worldbuilding functionality.

Do not add cloud dependencies unless explicitly authorized.

==================================================
28. AUTOSAVE
==================================================

The writer should never have to wonder:

"Did my work save?"

Provide a subtle status indicator.

Examples:

    Saved
    Saving...
    Changes saved
    Unable to save

Do not create intrusive notifications for every save.

Use the existing persistence mechanisms.

==================================================
29. ERROR UX
==================================================

Errors should be understandable to ordinary writers.

Avoid displaying raw exceptions where possible.

Bad:

    NullPointerException at Repository.kt:147

Better:

    "We couldn't save this change."

    [Retry]
    [Details]

Technical details can be available through a secondary option.

==================================================
30. MOBILE UX
==================================================

Mobile UI must prioritize:

    Writing
    Touch interaction
    Readability
    Compact navigation
    Bottom sheets
    Drawers
    Collapsible panels
    Floating actions where appropriate

Do not simply shrink the desktop UI.

Reorganize it responsively.

==================================================
31. DESKTOP UX
==================================================

Desktop UI may take advantage of:

    Sidebars
    Resizable panels
    Keyboard shortcuts
    Mouse interaction
    Drag and drop
    Larger graph/map views
    Multi-panel workspaces

Do not create a completely different application.

Maintain the same information architecture.

==================================================
32. MULTIPLATFORM PRINCIPLE
==================================================

The UI must be designed so the conceptual structure works across:

    Android
    Desktop
    Future platforms

The presentation may change.

The underlying interaction model should remain consistent.

Example:

DESKTOP:
    Persistent sidebar

MOBILE:
    Drawer/bottom sheet

Same function.
Different presentation.

==================================================
33. UI COMPONENT SYSTEM
==================================================

Create reusable components where appropriate.

Examples:

    StoryCard
    CharacterCard
    EntityCard
    RelationshipCard
    TimelineEventCard
    Sidebar
    QuickAdd
    SearchBar
    ContextMenu
    BottomSheet
    Dialog
    EmptyState
    LoadingState
    ErrorState
    SaveIndicator

Avoid duplicate implementations.

==================================================
34. EMPTY STATES
==================================================

Empty screens should explain what the writer can do next.

Example:

    No characters yet.

    Characters help you keep track of the
    people in your story.

    [+ Create Character]

Do not leave empty screens visually unexplained.

==================================================
35. FIRST-TIME EXPERIENCE
==================================================

The first launch should not overwhelm the writer.

Introduce:

    Create Story
    Simple Mode
    Complex Mode

Explain the difference briefly.

Do not force a long tutorial.

The user should be able to start writing immediately.

==================================================
36. UI DEVELOPMENT PROCESS
==================================================

Implement the frontend progressively.

PHASE 1
    Application shell
    Navigation
    Story Library
    Story Workspace

PHASE 2
    Writing Editor
    Chapters
    Scenes
    Focus Mode

PHASE 3
    Character UI
    Character Cards
    Character Editor

PHASE 4
    Worldbuilding UI
    Nations
    Locations
    Organizations
    Species
    Lore

PHASE 5
    Map integration
    Timeline integration
    Relationship integration

PHASE 6
    Story Sidebar
    Contextual information

PHASE 7
    Search
    Quick Add
    Command Palette

PHASE 8
    Settings
    Themes
    Custom Background

PHASE 9
    Reader Experience
    Export UI

PHASE 10
    Accessibility
    Mobile refinement
    Desktop refinement
    Performance refinement

==================================================
37. IMPLEMENTATION DISCIPLINE
==================================================

For every UI task:

1. Inspect existing code.

2. Identify existing backend/domain functionality.

3. Identify reusable UI components.

4. Implement only the requested UI functionality.

5. Connect it to existing backend interfaces.

6. Compile.

7. Run relevant tests.

8. Fix errors.

9. Verify existing functionality has not regressed.

10. Continue to the next task only after successful verification.

Do not perform large unrelated refactors.

==================================================
38. DESIGN DECISION RULE
==================================================

When there are multiple possible implementations, prefer:

    Simpler
    More reusable
    More accessible
    More responsive
    More platform-neutral
    Less resource-intensive
    Less intrusive
    More consistent with existing architecture

Do not choose complexity merely because the feature is technically possible.

==================================================
39. PERFORMANCE
==================================================

LoreCanvas should remain lightweight.

Avoid unnecessary:

    Continuous animations
    Background computation
    Heavy visual effects
    Constant graph recalculation
    Excessive recomposition
    Large image processing
    Unnecessary database operations

Especially optimize for mobile devices.

Custom backgrounds must not cause excessive memory usage.

Maps and graphs should load efficiently.

==================================================
40. FINAL UX PRINCIPLE
==================================================

LoreCanvas should feel like:

    "A writing application that can grow into a complete
     worldbuilding environment."

It should NOT feel like:

    "A worldbuilding database that happens to contain
     a text editor."

Writing remains the central activity.

Worldbuilding is powerful but optional.

Complexity should be available without being mandatory.

==================================================
41. CLAUDE EXECUTION RULES
==================================================

When working on this specification:

DO:
- inspect the repository,
- inspect existing backend APIs,
- reuse existing systems,
- implement incrementally,
- compile frequently,
- test frequently,
- preserve completed functionality,
- keep UI components reusable,
- maintain multiplatform compatibility.

DO NOT:
- rewrite the backend,
- replace repositories,
- duplicate domain models,
- invent unsupported APIs,
- remove existing functionality,
- add unrequested features,
- perform unrelated refactors,
- generate enormous explanations instead of implementing the task.

If something is ambiguous:

1. Inspect existing implementation.
2. Check this specification.
3. Prefer the least invasive interpretation.
4. If the ambiguity could affect architecture or data integrity, STOP and ask.

==================================================
42. REQUIRED FINAL REPORT
==================================================

After completing each implementation task, respond using:

IMPLEMENTED
- Brief description

FILES CHANGED
- File
- File

BACKEND CHANGES
- None
OR
- Explicitly describe authorized changes

TESTS
- Test/compile performed
- Result

UI STATUS
- Complete / Partial / Blocked

BLOCKERS
- None
OR
- Description

NEXT TASK
- Suggested next implementation step

Keep this report concise.

Do not repeat this specification.
Do not provide unnecessary tutorials.
Do not describe code that was not changed.
```

## How I'd use this with Claude

I **wouldn't send this entire document alongside every individual task** if Claude already has it in the project.

Instead, treat this as the **UI/UX master document**.

Then each individual Claude request can be tiny:

```text
Read the LoreCanvas UI/UX Master Specification.

Current task:
PHASE 3, CHARACTER UI.

Implement the Character Review Card and Character Page.

Requirements:
- Follow the existing backend.
- Do not modify completed backend systems.
- Make the review card usable from the Story Sidebar.
- Make the full Character Page suitable for editing.
- Support Simple Mode and Complex Mode appropriately.
- Reuse existing domain/repository functionality.
- Compile and test after implementation.

Do not implement the next phase yet.
```

Then after Claude finishes:

```text
Proceed to the next UI task in the specification.

First inspect the current implementation and verify the previous UI work.

Do not modify completed backend functionality.
Implement only the next phase.
Compile and test.
Return the required concise report.
```

### One particularly important addition

I'd have Claude maintain a tiny file called something like:

**`UI_IMPLEMENTATION_STATE.md`**

with:

```text
CURRENT PHASE:
3

COMPLETED:
✓ Application shell
✓ Navigation
✓ Story Library
✓ Story Workspace
✓ Writing Editor
✓ Focus Mode
✓ Character Review Card

IN PROGRESS:
Character Page

NEXT:
Character Editor

BACKEND MODIFIED:
No

KNOWN ISSUES:
None
```

That way, if Claude's conversation hits its context limit again, you don't have to reconstruct the entire UI development history. The **project itself remembers where Claude stopped**.

This is particularly useful for LoreCanvas because we're deliberately building the UI in layers rather than asking Claude to generate the whole frontend in one enormous leap.

### **ASSISTANT** — 2026-08-13 07:08 UTC

The **testing phase** is the stage after Claude has implemented the backend and frontend. Its job is to answer one question:

> **"Does LoreCanvas actually work reliably as a real application, rather than merely compiling?"**

For LoreCanvas, I'd make testing a dedicated phase rather than just asking Claude to run a compile at the end.

## 🧪 LoreCanvas Testing Phase

I'd divide it into **7 layers**.

### 1. Backend testing

First verify that the foundation still works.

Test:

- Creating data
- Editing data
- Deleting data
- Saving data
- Loading data after restarting
- Repository operations
- Search
- Graph/relationships
- Timeline
- Map data
- Commands
- Undo/redo
- Storage
- Import/export
- Error handling

For example:

```text
Create Character
       ↓
Save
       ↓
Close application
       ↓
Reopen
       ↓
Character still exists
```

This catches one of the nastiest classes of bugs: **"It worked until I restarted the app."**

---

# 2. Frontend/UI testing

Then test every major screen.

### Story

- Create story
- Open story
- Rename story
- Delete story
- Switch between stories
- Continue writing

### Editor

- Write text
- Edit text
- Undo/redo
- Create chapter
- Create scene
- Save
- Reopen

### Characters

- Create character
- Edit character
- Delete character
- View character card
- View full character
- Create relationship

### World

- Create nation
- Create location
- Create organization
- Create species
- Create lore

### Map

- Create map
- Add locations
- Select locations
- Edit information
- Save
- Reopen

### Timeline

- Create event
- Edit event
- Move event
- Connect relevant entities
- Save/reopen

### Sidebar

- Open
- Close
- Switch sections
- Open character
- Open map
- Open timeline
- Return to story

---

# 3. Integration testing

This is **especially important for LoreCanvas**.

We don't just want to know:

> "Does the character page work?"

We want to know:

> **"Does the character page work with everything else?"**

For example:

```text
Character
   ↓
Relationship
   ↓
Timeline Event
   ↓
Location
   ↓
Map
   ↓
Story
   ↓
Story Sidebar
```

If you create:

**Elara → Arclight → Siege of Arclight**

then LoreCanvas should correctly connect those pieces wherever the UI expects them.

This is where we discover broken links between systems.

---

# 4. Simple Mode / Complex Mode testing

This deserves its own test category.

### Simple Mode

A new writer should be able to:

```text
Open LoreCanvas
       ↓
Create Story
       ↓
Start Writing
```

without being forced to create:

- Characters
- Maps
- Nations
- Timeline
- Magic systems
- Relationships

### Complex Mode

The writer should be able to gradually build:

```text
Story
 ├── Characters
 ├── World
 │    ├── Nations
 │    ├── Locations
 │    ├── Organizations
 │    └── Species
 ├── Maps
 ├── Timeline
 └── Relationships
```

Then return to writing.

The two modes must **not produce incompatible stories**.

---

# 5. Performance testing

This is where we check your original goal of keeping LoreCanvas lightweight.

We should test progressively larger projects.

### Small

```text
1 story
10 characters
5 locations
20 timeline events
1 map
```

### Medium

```text
1 story
100 characters
100+ locations
500 timeline events
Several maps
Large relationship graph
```

### Large

Something intentionally ridiculous:

```text
Several stories
500+ characters
Hundreds of locations
Thousands of timeline events
Large maps
Large relationship graphs
Large story text
```

Then measure:

- Startup time
- Memory usage
- CPU usage
- UI responsiveness
- Map performance
- Graph performance
- Search performance
- Save/load time
- Export time

We don't necessarily need LoreCanvas to handle the ridiculous case beautifully, but it should **fail gracefully rather than collapse into a smoking toaster**.

---

# 6. Device/platform testing

Once the application is stable, test it on actual devices.

For Android:

### Low-end device

Check:

- startup
- writing
- scrolling
- map
- timeline
- search
- memory
- battery consumption

### Mid-range device

Same tests.

### High-end device

Same tests.

Then desktop once the multiplatform frontend exists.

The goal isn't:

> "Does it technically install?"

It's:

> **"Does it feel usable on different hardware?"**

---

# 7. Real-world user testing

This is the final boss.

You use LoreCanvas **as an actual writer**, rather than as its developer.

Create a completely new fictional story from scratch.

For example:

```text
Create story
    ↓
Simple Mode
    ↓
Write several chapters
    ↓
Create characters
    ↓
Switch to Complex Mode
    ↓
Create nations
    ↓
Create locations
    ↓
Build map
    ↓
Create timeline
    ↓
Create relationships
    ↓
Return to writing
    ↓
Use Story Sidebar
    ↓
Read the story
    ↓
Export it
    ↓
Close LoreCanvas
    ↓
Reopen it
```

Then deliberately try to break it.

Delete things.

Undo things.

Restart the app.

Create strange names.

Use huge amounts of text.

Import large images.

Move things around.

Try things in an order the developers didn't anticipate.

That's where the **real bugs live**.

---

# The final testing cycle

I'd structure the entire phase like this:

```text
                 TESTING PHASE
                       │
          ┌────────────┼────────────┐
          ↓            ↓            ↓
       Backend       Frontend    Integration
          │            │            │
          └────────────┼────────────┘
                       ↓
                Mode Testing
                       ↓
               Performance
                       ↓
             Platform Testing
                       ↓
              Real User Testing
                       ↓
                  BUG FIXING
                       ↓
                  RETESTING
                       ↓
                 RELEASE BUILD
```

And importantly, **bug fixing doesn't mean immediately changing everything**.

For every bug:

```text
Bug discovered
      ↓
Reproduce it
      ↓
Identify cause
      ↓
Fix smallest appropriate component
      ↓
Compile
      ↓
Run affected test
      ↓
Run regression tests
      ↓
Confirm fix
```

## When do we actually call LoreCanvas "finished"?

Not when Claude says:

> "Implementation complete."

Not when the project compiles.

I'd call the **first release candidate** ready when:

- Backend tests pass
- Frontend tests pass
- Integration tests pass
- Simple Mode works
- Complex Mode works
- Saving/loading works reliably
- Maps work
- Timeline works
- Relationships work
- Story Sidebar works
- Export works
- Custom backgrounds work
- No major data-loss bugs remain
- Performance is acceptable on target devices
- A complete story can be created from beginning to export without manually repairing the application

Then we can move from **development → testing → bug fixing → release preparation**.

And I'd actually make the testing phase its own Claude instruction document, just like the UI/UX master specification, so Claude has a formal checklist instead of simply being told "test the app."
